overview.title: Student & Teacher Overview: Lesson 15
overview.text: This lesson has two main purposes: The first is to continue the work from Lessons 11—13 regarding the interplay among graphs, equations, and functions; the second is to expose students to piecewise functions in general and the absolute value and step functions specifically. Lessons 12 and 13 established the meaning of the graph of a function and the graph of the equation y=f(x). This lesson continues to clarify that these two sets are one and the same. Students consider two important functions used in later lessons and classes: the absolute value function and the greatest integer function.
outcomes: Students examine the features of piecewise functions, including the absolute value function and step functions.
Students understand that the graph of a function f is the graph of the equation y=f(x).
overview.teacherInsight: Emphasize precise mathematical definitions and multiple problem-solving representations. Encourage students to check the reasonableness of their numerical solutions.

guidedExercises.title: Example 1: Core Mathematical Modeling for Piecewise Functions
guidedExercises.problem: Classwork Opening (2 minutes) Recall that the absolute value of a number is the distance from 0 of a point on the number line. Because distance is being measured, the absolute value of a nonzero number is always positive. For example, (-3)=3 because the point -3, located 3 units to the left of 0 on the real number line, is 3 units away from 0. problems.prompt: Explain why the sawtooth function, sawtooth(x)=x-(x) for all real numbers x, takes only the fractional part of a number when the number is positive.
problems.solution: If you subtract the integer part of a number from the number, only the fractional par" will remain.

problems.prompt:
The Heaviside function is defined using the formula below.

H(x)=(-1,x<00,x=01,x>0)

Graph this function, and state its domain and range.

The following piecewise function is an example of a step function.

S(x)=(3 -5≤x<-21-2≤x<32 3≤x≤5)

Graph this function, and state the domain and range.
Why is this type of function called a step function?
problems.solution: The horizontal line segments step up and down like steps.

problems.prompt:
Let f(x)=\frac{(x)}{x}, where x can be any real number except 0.

Why is the number 0 excluded from the domain of f?
problems.solution: If x=0, then the expression would not be defined.

problems.prompt: What is the range of f?

Create a graph of f.

Express f as a piecewise function.
What is the difference between this function and the Heaviside function?
problems.solution: The domain of the Heaviside function is all real numbers. The Heaviside function has a value of 0 when x=0. This function excludes the real number 0 from the domain.
